concepts.definition: A copper cable with integrated retimer chips at each end that regenerate digital signals electronically, extending the useful reach of copper interconnects inside server racks. AECs compete with pluggable optical transceivers for short-reach GPU-to-GPU connections in AI training clusters, and have gained significant share because CPO is not yet available at volume.

An infrastructure operator that provides raw compute or power-dense colocation facilities without a proprietary software layer, often a repurposed bitcoin miner. Capacity plays rely on hyperscaler lease agreements for revenue and are subject to dilutive equity offerings to fund capital expenditure, limiting compounding for existing shareholders.

In Serenity’s taxonomy, a bottleneck is a near-term supply squeeze tied to demand exceeding existing capacity — solvable with capex and time. A chokepoint is a structural process-IP position that persists across multiple technology generations, where even well-funded competition faces multi-year customer qualification cycles before becoming viable. AXT (AXTI) is classified a bottleneck; LPKF (LPK.DE) and Soitec (SOI.PA) are classified chokepoints.

A packaging architecture in which optical transceivers are integrated directly onto the same substrate as the compute or switching chip, replacing pluggable modules. CPO dramatically reduces the power consumed in moving data across a rack and is central to NVIDIA's Spectrum-X Photonics and Quantum-X Photonics switch programmes.

A data-centre hosting model in which the facility operator provides power, space, and physical infrastructure while the customer — typically a hyperscaler — installs and owns the servers and networking equipment. Colocation operators earn lease income without bearing GPU ownership or replacement risk.

The manufacturing step in which a completed HBM die stack is sealed inside an epoxy compound using a press that applies the resin from above under controlled pressure and temperature, rather than injecting it from the side as in transfer molding. Compression molding is preferred for HBM because it applies lower mechanical stress to the thin stacked dies and achieves better surface flatness, which is critical for subsequent bonding to the GPU interposer.

TSMC's advanced 2.5D packaging platform that places multiple chiplets — GPU logic, HBM memory stacks, and increasingly photonic dies — side by side on a shared silicon interposer, which is then mounted on a conventional organic substrate. CoWoS allows far shorter electrical distances between chips than a standard PCB, enabling the high bandwidth required by modern AI accelerators.

An architecture that integrates optical transceivers — the devices that convert electrical signals to photons for transmission over fibre — directly onto the same package substrate as the processor, rather than in a separate pluggable module. CPO reduces latency by roughly 10x and power consumption by roughly half at equivalent bandwidth, and is considered the likely successor to pluggable optics in hyperscale AI data centres from 2026 onwards.

Compute Unified Device Architecture: Nvidia’s proprietary parallel-computing platform and programming model. Because virtually all AI frameworks and models are optimised for CUDA, switching to non-Nvidia accelerators requires substantial engineering investment, creating deep customer lock-in.

An InP laser whose cavity includes a periodic grating that selects a single emission wavelength. DFB lasers are the dominant light source in data-centre transceivers because their narrow linewidth and stable wavelength allow dense wavelength-division multiplexing, packing multiple data channels onto a single fibre.

Chipmaking process that uses 13.5-nanometre light to print the finest circuit features on leading-edge semiconductors. ASML is the sole manufacturer of EUV machines; every advanced AI chip depends on them.

A neocloud that goes beyond bare GPU rental to provide software orchestration, managed storage, inference endpoints, and developer tooling. The full-stack model generates higher gross margins than raw capacity provision because customers pay for software value on top of hardware, creating switching costs that pure capacity providers lack.

Serenity's term for a supplier that occupies a chokepoint in a technology supply chain with no credible near-term substitute, regardless of its size. The argument is that a hyperscaler will pay a ransom-like premium for such components once a product cycle depends on them, making standard valuation multiples irrelevant.

A stacked DRAM standard used in AI accelerators and networking ASICs that requires the memory die to be bonded directly to the logic chip. HBM4, standardised by JEDEC in April 2025, supports up to 2 TB/s of bandwidth. Towa Corporation (6315.T) supplies the compression-moulding tools used in HBM packaging.

The fourth generation of high-bandwidth memory, used primarily in AI accelerators. HBM4 requires compression moulding of stacked DRAM dies into a single package — the process step TOWA Corporation dominates globally, with Micron, SK Hynix, and Samsung as primary customers.

The strategic reorientation of a cryptocurrency mining company toward high-performance computing and AI workloads. Miners have power infrastructure and data-centre facilities that can be redeployed to host AI GPUs; the pivot requires either purchasing GPUs directly or signing colocation agreements with hyperscalers who supply the hardware.

A die-stacking technique that forms direct copper-to-copper electrical connections between dies without solder bumps, enabling interconnect pitches below 4 microns — roughly 10x finer than current micro-bump technology. Hybrid bonding is the roadmap path for HBM4E and beyond, promising higher bandwidth density and lower power consumption per bit transferred between the memory and logic dies.

The options market's forward-looking estimate of how much an asset will move, derived from current option prices rather than historical data. Low implied volatility signals that options are relatively cheap, making them attractive to buyers who anticipate an eventual large move the market has not yet priced in.

A compound semiconductor material preferred for the lasers and photodetectors in high-speed optical transceivers, because silicon cannot generate light efficiently. AXT (AXTI) and Lumentum (LITE) are key players in its supply chain. China added InP to its export-control list in February 2025, creating the supply shock that drove AXTI's price from roughly $12 to over $80.

A die that has been tested and burned-in at the wafer level before being diced and assembled into a multi-chip package. KGD screening is increasingly important as CoWoS packages become more expensive: assembling a defective die into a package worth hundreds or thousands of dollars destroys the value of all the other known-good components in that package.

LPKF’s proprietary laser process for drilling fine-pitch through-glass vias in glass core substrates — the advanced-packaging layer that succeeds organic ABF cores in high-density interconnect applications. The technology’s long qualification cycle and IP secrecy are the primary basis for LPKF’s chokepoint claim in the next packaging transition.

Long-term Equity AnticiPation Securities — exchange-listed options contracts with expiration dates more than one year away. Traders use them to express directional views with defined downside risk and embedded leverage, particularly when expecting slow-moving macro trends to play out over a multi-year horizon.

A GPU-specialist cloud provider that rents NVIDIA accelerator capacity to AI developers and research labs, sitting between the chip manufacturers and the frontier labs. Unlike the major hyperscalers, neoclouds do not offer a broad service catalogue; their value proposition is fast access to large volumes of GPU compute, often under long-term contracts.

A qubit architecture that encodes quantum information in individual neutral atoms held in optical tweezers generated by lasers, as opposed to superconducting or trapped-ion approaches. Proponents argue it scales more cleanly to larger arrays and operates at room temperature, avoiding the extreme cooling needed by superconducting rivals.

A long-term contract between a power generator and a buyer — typically a hyperscaler or data-centre operator — fixing the price and volume of electricity delivery over periods of 10–20 years. Nuclear PPAs are particularly sought after because they guarantee baseload, carbon-free power at predictable cost, satisfying both reliability and sustainability requirements for AI data centres.

Thin copper wiring layers deposited on an interposer or reconstituted wafer that route electrical signals between the fine-pitch bumps of a chiplet and the coarser-pitch bumps that connect to the organic substrate. In CoWoS interposers, multiple RDL layers carry high-density signal routing between GPU logic and HBM stacks; their fabrication requires precise copper plating and etch steps.

An open-source instruction-set architecture originated at UC Berkeley in 2010 and now governed by RISC-V International, a Swiss non-profit. Unlike proprietary architectures such as Arm, anyone can implement a RISC-V chip without licensing fees. RocketChip, mentioned by Serenity, is the Berkeley RISC-V processor generator that became foundational to the ecosystem.

Semiconductor IP that converts parallel data streams to high-speed serial links for chip-to-chip and chip-to-optic interconnects inside data centres. Marvell is a leading supplier of high-speed SerDes for AI networking.

A wafer structure in which a thin crystalline silicon layer (typically 220 nm for photonics) sits atop an electrically insulating buried oxide. The index contrast between the silicon device layer and the oxide below confines light within the waveguide, which is essential for low-loss optical routing on a photonic chip.

A technology that uses silicon-based waveguides to guide and modulate light on a chip, enabling high-speed, low-power optical data links between processors. Because silicon is transparent to infrared light and compatible with standard semiconductor fabrication, it allows optical functions to be integrated alongside electronics on the same wafer.

Soitec's proprietary wafer-engineering process that uses hydrogen-ion implantation to cleave a precisely controlled thin layer from a donor silicon wafer, then bonds it by molecular adhesion onto a handle wafer. It is the only technique capable of producing photonics-grade SOI with the sub-nanometre thickness uniformity required across 300mm wafers at commercial volumes.

A Special Purpose Acquisition Company is a listed blank-cheque vehicle that raises money in an IPO solely to acquire a private target. The merger with that target serves as the de facto public listing for the operating company, often at a pre-negotiated valuation and with less regulatory scrutiny than a traditional IPO.

A vertical electrical connection drilled through a silicon die and filled with copper, allowing signals and power to pass between stacked dies without routing around the chip edge. TSVs are the enabling technology for HBM stacking: each DRAM die in a stack has thousands of TSVs that must be formed, inspected and precisely aligned before bonding.

A chip designed from scratch for a specific hyperscaler’s AI workloads, as opposed to a commodity GPU. Google’s TPU, Microsoft’s Maia, and Amazon’s Trainium are all XPUs. Marvell designs and manufactures XPUs for hyperscalers under long-term supply agreements.
